stories.story_title: How Netomi Scales Enterprise AI Agents with OpenAI Architecture
stories.why_this_story: Scaling autonomous AI agents in enterprise production requires moving beyond single prompts to multi-step reasoning, concurrency, and real-time governance layers.
stories.viral_angle: Most AI agents fail in production because they rely on single prompts. Netomi built a concurrent governance framework that makes AI agents reliable at scale.
stories.story_sentence: Everyone thinks scaling AI agents is about better prompting, but Netomi proved enterprise reliability requires deterministic software guardrails around LLMs.
stories.story_arc: Hook → Challenge → Architecture → Escalation → Pattern Interrupt → Implication → Payoff

design.visual_strategy: Technical editorial breakdown using structured diagram blocks, editorial metadata, and clear visual hierarchy to explain enterprise agent architecture.
design.retention_strategy: Maintain high visual momentum by shifting from problem identification to architecture diagrams, followed by a dark pattern interrupt slide highlighting the core key metric.

source_story.title: Netomi’s lessons for scaling agentic systems into the enterprise

slides.headline: HOW AI AGENTS ACTUALLY SCALE
slides.body: Netomi automates millions of enterprise customer interactions. Here is how they built multi-step AI agents that do not fail in production.
slides.visual_concept: Oversized bold grotesk headline paired with precise technical metadata tags and structured brand rule lines.
slides.asset_requirement: Official case study banner image or high-contrast editorial headline layout.
slides.implication: Single-prompt systems are obsolete for critical business operations.
slides.swipe_reason: Sets up an unanswered engineering question about agent reliability.

slides.headline: THE SINGLE-PROMPT LIMIT
slides.body: Standard LLM implementations attempt to solve complex multi-step tasks in one shot. In enterprise workflows, a single hallucination destroys system trust.
slides.visual_concept: Linear flowchart showing a single LLM prompt breaking at step three due to context loss.
slides.asset_requirement: Diagram comparing fragile single-prompt execution versus multi-step orchestration.
slides.context: Failure modes in autonomous customer service agents.
slides.implication: Linear prompting cannot handle non-deterministic business logic.
slides.swipe_reason: Creates tension by exposing the primary cause of AI project failures.

slides.headline: CONCURRENCY + REASONING
slides.body: Netomi orchestrates multi-step workflows by pairing advanced OpenAI models with concurrent execution pathways, validating actions before execution.
slides.visual_concept: Bento card showing concurrent agent pipelines executing tasks parallel to automated governance checks.
slides.asset_requirement: System diagram showing multi-agent reasoning and orchestration flow.
slides.implication: Reliability comes from architecture, not model parameter count alone.
slides.swipe_reason: Delivers real engineering evidence validating the solutions.

slides.headline: ZERO UNCHECKED ACTIONS
slides.body: Every automated action passes real-time policy checks. If confidence scores fall below threshold, the agent seamlessly routes the task to human teams.
slides.visual_concept: Threshold indicator widget showing automated confidence scoring and dynamic human-in-the-loop handoff triggers.
slides.asset_requirement: Visual threshold callout for human-in-the-loop fallback mechanism.
slides.context: Risk management in enterprise autonomous workflows.
slides.implication: Autonomous systems must integrate graceful degradation paths.
slides.swipe_reason: Demonstrates how top enterprises eliminate operational risks.

slides.headline: PREDICTABILITY OVER SPEED
slides.body: In enterprise agentic systems, deterministic system guardrails around LLMs matter more than raw speed or speculative intelligence.
slides.visual_concept: Dark ink background with high-contrast cream typography and subtle mint accents creating a visual break.
slides.asset_requirement: Dark contrast pattern interrupt slide focusing purely on core architecture takeaway.
slides.implication: Software engineering fundamentals remain essential in the AI stack.
slides.swipe_reason: High visual contrast re-engages user attention for final takeaways.

slides.headline: THE NEW AI STACK
slides.body: Building production AI isn't just about prompt engineering. It requires building robust traditional software wrappers to govern probabilistic models.
slides.visual_concept: Two-column comparison showing 'Probabilistic Model Core' wrapped by 'Deterministic Software Rules'.
slides.asset_requirement: Clean comparison breakdown of probabilistic vs deterministic control layers.
slides.context: Shift in developer roles from pure prompting to hybrid agent system design.
slides.implication: Developers must focus on state management, governance, and evaluation frameworks.
slides.swipe_reason: Translates complex architecture into actionable engineering strategy.

slides.headline: AGENTS ARE SOFTWARE SYSTEMS
slides.body: The future of enterprise AI isn't standalone autonomous models. It is disciplined software architecture giving models precise operational boundaries.
slides.visual_concept: Minimalist editorial summary card with brand tag: GETBYTERUSH • TESTED • EXPLAINED • REAL.
slides.asset_requirement: Final takeaway layout featuring signature brand mark.
slides.context: Final verdict on building enterprise-grade agentic AI.
slides.implication: Enterprise AI success depends on software discipline, not magic prompts.
slides.swipe_reason: Provides a definitive and memorable takeaway worth saving and sharing.
